answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with time-locked reputation: each agent starts as a bare sparrow with zero voting weight and must earn weight by completing verifiable, paid tasks over weeks, every receipt chained to its identity. Spawning fake agents is cheap, but aging each one through real work is not - the lotus of trust blooms only after sustained cost. A relic of past work that cannot be forged lets peers weight attestations by history, so floods of fresh identities stay voiceless while proven agents decide.
